title: Boeing FY2022 Form 10-K — Critical Accounting Policies: Program Accounting requires estimating "gross profit margin" for a defined program accounting quantity
key_points: Program accounting "requires the demonstrated ability to reliably estimate revenues, costs and gross profit margin for the defined program accounting quantity."

A program is defined as the estimated number of units (the accounting quantity), so gross margin is an estimate spread across a multi-unit, multi-year block rather than a period-level revenue-minus-COGS residual.
Revenue and cost estimates for all significant long-term contract performance obligations are reviewed and reassessed quarterly.
Changes in estimates can result in cumulative catch-up adjustments to the performance obligation's inception-to-date revenues, cost of sales and profits.

Cumulative catch-up adjustments increased Loss from operations by $5,253M in 2022, $880M in 2021 and $942M in 2020, driven primarily in 2022 by losses on VC-25B, KC-46A Tanker, MQ-25, Commercial Crew and T-7A Red Hawk — all described as fixed-price development programs.
A 1% change in combined estimated gross margins on profitable long-term contracts would have changed 2022 pre-tax income by approximately $300M.
raw_excerpt: Program Accounting requires the demonstrated ability to reliably estimate revenues, costs and gross profit margin for the defined program accounting quantity. A program consists of the estimated number of units (accountin[g quantity])... Changes in these estimates could result in recognition of cumulative catch-up adjustments to the performance obligation's inception to date revenues, cost of sales and prof[its] ... increased Loss from operations by $5,253 million, $880 million and $942 million in 2022, 2021 and 2020, respectively. The cumulative catch-up adjustments in 2022 were primarily due to losses recognized on the VC-25B, KC-46A Tanker, MQ-25, Commercial Crew and T-7A Red Hawk programs. These are all fixed-price development programs ... combined gross margins for our profitable long-term contracts had been estimated to be higher or lower by 1% during 2022, it would have increased or decreased pre-tax income for the year by approximately $300 million.

title: Boeing FY2022 Form 10-K — Program-level margin disclosures: 777X "near break-even gross margins"; 787 accounting-quantity increase "improved the program's profit margin"
key_points: "The 777X program had near break-even gross margins at December 31, 2022."

Boeing states that one or more factors (production disruption, customer negotiations, production rate adjustments, contraction of the accounting quantity, certification timing) could result in additional reach-forward losses on the 777X program in future periods.

In Q4 2022 Boeing increased the 787 accounting quantity by 100 units, and states that "the increase in the accounting quantity improved the program's profit margin" — i.e., program margin is a function of the assumed unit block, not of period volume.

Boeing determined in Q3 2021 that 787 production rates below 5 per month were abnormally low and that excessive inspection and rework costs on inventoried aircraft must be accounted for as abnormal production costs expensed as incurred.

Cumulative 787 abnormal costs recorded through December 31, 2022 totaled $1.7 billion; in Q4 2022 Boeing raised the total estimate of abnormal production costs to $2.8 billion, most to be incurred by end of 2023 (prior expectation at Dec 31, 2021 was approximately $2 billion).
Boeing recorded a $3.5 billion loss on the 787 program in Q4 2021 primarily due to additional rework and other actions required to resume deliveries taking longer than expected.
raw_excerpt: The 777X program had near break-even gross margins at December 31, 2022. ... 787 Program During the fourth quarter of 2022, we increased the accounting quantity for the 787 program by 100 units due to the program's normal progress of obtaining additional orders and delivering aircraft. The increase in the accounting quantity improved the program's profit margin. ... In the third quarter of 2021, we determined that production rates below 5 per month represented abnormally low production rates and result in abnormal production costs. We also determined that the inspections and rework costs on inventoried aircraft are excessive and should also be accounted for as abnormal production costs that are required to be expensed as incurred. Cumulative abnormal costs recorded through December 31, 2022 totaled $1.7 billion. During the fourth quarter of 2022 we adjusted the total estimate of abnormal production costs up to $2.8 billion with most being incurred by the end of 2023.

title: Boeing FY2022 Form 10-K — Reach-forward losses recorded as a reduction to deferred production costs (787 $3,460M; 777X $6,493M)
key_points: In Q4 2021 Boeing determined that estimated costs to complete the 787 program plus costs already in 787 inventory exceeded estimated revenues, and "the resulting reach-forward loss of $3,460 was recorded as a reduction to deferred production costs."

At December 31, 2022 the 787 program carried deferred production costs of $12,689M (vs $11,693M at Dec 31, 2021), supplier advances of $1,831M and unamortized tooling and other non-recurring costs of $1,722M.

Of the 787 deferred production costs and unamortized tooling/non-recurring costs, $9,881M is expected to be recovered from units in the program accounting quantity with firm orders and $4,530M from units representing expected future orders.
787 abnormal production costs expensed were $1,240M in 2022 and $468M in 2021, because Boeing is producing at abnormally low rates.
The April 2022 decision to pause 777X-9 production during 2022 and 2023 results in abnormal production costs expensed as incurred; $325M was expensed in 2022.
"The 777X program has near break-even margins at December 31, 2022."
Commercial aircraft programs inventory included early issue sales consideration credited to airline customers of $3,586M (2022) and $3,290M (2021).
raw_excerpt: During the fourth quarter of 2021, we determined that estimated costs to complete the 787 program plus costs already included in 787 inventory exceed estimated revenues from the program. The resulting reach-forward loss of $3,460 was recorded as a reduction to deferred production costs. ... At December 31, 2022, $9,881 of 787 deferred production costs, unamortized tooling and other non-recurring costs are expected to be recovered from units included in the program accounting quantity that have firm orders, and $4,530 is expected to be recovered from units included in the program accounting quantity that represent expected future orders. ... We expensed abnormal production costs of $1,240 and $468 during the years ended December 31, 2022 and 2021. ... The production pause is resulting in abnormal production costs that are being expensed as incurred until 777X-9 production resumes. We expensed abnormal production costs of $325 during the year ended December 31, 2022.

title: The Boeing Company 2022 Form 10-K — Program Accounting policy & accounting quantities (Critical Accounting Policies; Note 1; Program Highlights)
key_points: Program accounting requires the demonstrated ability to reliably estimate revenues, costs and gross profit margin for the defined program accounting quantity; a program consists of the estimated number of units (accounting quantity).

The accounting quantity includes delivered units, undelivered units under contract, and units anticipated to be under contract in the reasonable future (anticipated orders); all of these must be considered in developing total program estimates.
During Q4 2022 Boeing increased the 787 accounting quantity by 100 units due to normal progress in obtaining orders and delivering aircraft, and the increase improved the program's profit margin.
The determination of the accounting quantity is limited by the ability to make reasonably dependable estimates.

title: The Boeing Company 2022 Form 10-K — Reach-forward loss mechanics and cumulative catch-up adjustments (Critical Accounting Policies; BDS results)
key_points: Reductions to an estimated program loss are included in the gross profit margin for undelivered units in the accounting quantity, whereas increases to the estimated loss are recorded as an earnings charge in the period in which the loss is determined.

Net cumulative catch-up adjustments for changes in estimated revenues and costs at completion across all long-term contracts, including the impact of increases in estimated losses on unexercised options, increased Loss from operations by $5,253 million in 2022, $880 million in 2021 and $942 million in 2020.

Fixed-price development program charges recorded in 2022 at BDS: VC-25B $1,452 million, KC-46A Tanker $1,374 million, MQ-25 $579 million, T-7A Red Hawk Production Options $552 million, T-7A Red Hawk EMD $203 million, Commercial Crew $288 million.

BDS cumulative contract catch-up adjustments in 2022 were $4,284 million more unfavorable than 2021; BDS recorded a loss from operations of $3,544 million in 2022 versus earnings of $1,544 million in 2021.
Significant adjustments during the three years ended December 31, 2022 included losses on VC-25B, KC-46A Tanker, MQ-25, Commercial Crew and T-7A Red Hawk programs.
If the combined gross margins for profitable long-term contracts had been estimated higher or lower by 1% during 2022, pre-tax income would have changed by approximately $300 million.
